# DoneGuard

> Blocks AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) from ending their turn until the
> project's checks pass.

DoneGuard is a single static Go binary. It registers itself on the Stop and
SubagentStop hooks. When the agent tries to stop, it runs the verify commands from
.doneguard.yml (tests, lint, type-check) and checks, via git, that no protected paths
(.env, keys, secrets) were touched. On failure the stop is blocked and the agent gets
the failing command and its output, up to a retry cap (default 3, max 7); after that
the stop is allowed and logged as UNVERIFIED. DoneGuard makes no network calls.

Repository: https://github.com/mkarvan/doneguard
Full agent guide: https://github.com/mkarvan/doneguard/blob/main/AGENTS.md
README: https://github.com/mkarvan/doneguard/blob/main/README.md

## Install into a user's project (non-interactive, safe to re-run)

1. Get the binary. If you cannot get a working `doneguard version`, STOP: do not run
   init or install and do not edit the project; tell the user what failed.

   a. If `doneguard version` already exits 0, use it.

   b. Else, if `go version` reports Go 1.23 or newer:
        go install github.com/mkarvan/doneguard/cmd/doneguard@latest &&
          export PATH="$(go env GOPATH)/bin:$PATH" &&
          doneguard version
      (if `go env GOBIN` is set, put it on PATH too). Nonzero exit: try c.

   c. Else (Linux/macOS amd64/arm64, no sudo, HTTPS only, SHA-256 verified), download
      the script to a file, check the download, then run it and check that too.
      Agents: do not pipe it into sh.
        dg_tmp=$(mktemp -d) &&
          curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' -o "$dg_tmp/install.sh" \
            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkarvan/doneguard/main/scripts/install.sh
        (nonzero exit: stop; optionally read "$dg_tmp/install.sh")
        sh "$dg_tmp/install.sh" &&
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" &&
          doneguard version
        (nonzero exit: stop)
      The script installs to ~/.local/bin/doneguard and exits nonzero if the download,
      checksum or the installed binary's `version` fails. Optional:
      DONEGUARD_VERSION=v0.1.0 pins a release; DONEGUARD_BIN_DIR changes the install
      directory. Humans who have read the script may use `curl -fsSL <url> | sh`.

   Required: `doneguard version` exits 0 and prints a version. Re-export PATH in later
   steps if each command runs in a fresh shell.

2. cd to the root of the user's project (a git repository). If it isn't one, only
   `git init` when that is clearly appropriate; otherwise tell the user (protected-path
   checks need git) and continue.

3. Create the config (auto-detects verify commands; keeps an existing config file,
   exit 0; exits nonzero if .doneguard.yml/.yaml is a directory or dangling symlink:
   stop and tell the user):
     doneguard init --yes

4. Register the hooks for the agent in use:
     doneguard install --agent claude    # Claude Code -> .claude/settings.json
     doneguard install --agent codex     # Codex CLI   -> .codex/hooks.json
     doneguard install                   # both / not sure
   install is idempotent and never touches other hooks or settings.

## Verify

  doneguard version
  doneguard report    (optional; empty until the first stop)

Check the JSON, not just a grep: .claude/settings.json (and/or .codex/hooks.json) must
have, under BOTH hooks.Stop and hooks.SubagentStop, a hook with "type": "command" and
"command": "<absolute path>/doneguard hook --source claude" (or --source codex).
With jq (exits 0 only if both events have it; use codex / .codex/hooks.json for Codex):
  jq -e --arg src claude '. as $r | all("Stop", "SubagentStop"; . as $e |
    any($r.hooks[$e][]?.hooks[]?; .type == "command" and
      (.command | test("doneguard\\x27? hook --source " + $src + "$"))))' .claude/settings.json
If an event is missing, re-run `doneguard install`; don't hand-edit.

Then tell the user:
- Claude Code: restart Claude Code so the hooks load (check with /hooks).
- Codex: trust the project and approve the hook. These are separate:
  `codex exec --trust` saves project trust; approving happens in /hooks;
  `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` skips hook review for one run and is only for
  automation that has already vetted the hook. See "Codex hook trust" in the README.

## Uninstall

  doneguard uninstall                  (or --agent claude / --agent codex)
Removes only DoneGuard's hook entries.

## Do not

- Hand-edit .claude/settings.json or .codex/hooks.json to add hooks; use
  doneguard install / doneguard uninstall.
- Commit .doneguard/ (session logs, retry state; init gitignores it). Do commit
  .doneguard.yml.
- Use `doneguard init --force` unless the user explicitly asked to overwrite the config.
- Put secrets in the hook command or the config.
- Run `doneguard install --global` unless the user asked.
- Weaken .doneguard.yml to get past a blocked stop; fix the failing check instead.
